title.en: JANUS Connection — Linear A: Structure Before Semantics
title.ru: JANUS Connection — Линейное А: структура до семантики

important_external_facts.partial_phonetic_values: Approximate sound values for many Linear A syllabic signs are inferred from homomorphic Linear B signs; these values are useful but do not constitute a complete decipherment.
important_external_facts.contextual_support: Some inferred readings align with contextual expectations such as proposed place names, but the underlying language remains unidentified and many readings remain debated.
important_external_facts.unique_logograms: Approximately 80% of Linear A logograms are reported as not appearing in Linear B.
important_external_facts.formulaic_structure: Linear A inscriptions include recurring standardized formulas, including the so-called libation formula, which can be studied structurally even though the language is not fully deciphered.
important_external_facts.directionality: Linear A is predominantly written left-to-right, with occasional right-to-left and rare boustrophedon examples; directionality alone is not a semantic decipherment.

connection.name: STRUCTURE_BEFORE_SEMANTICS
connection.core_observation: A writing system can retain strong, analyzable structural regularities even when its underlying language and full semantics remain undeciphered.
connection.mechanism: RAW_SIGNS -> SHAPE_RELATIONS -> REPETITION/FORMULA -> CONTEXT -> PROVISIONAL_INTERPRETATION -> CLAIM_CEILING
connection.why_non_obvious: The common mistake is to collapse undeciphered into unknowable. Linear A demonstrates a narrower epistemic state: substantial structural knowledge can coexist with semantic uncertainty.
connection.claim_ceiling: This is a methodological analogy, not a decipherment of Linear A and not evidence that any JANUS registry object is encoded in Linear A.

registry_connections.observation: Tranception retrieves homologous sequences and uses related structures as evidence while preserving a boundary between inferred fitness and universal truth. Linear A similarly permits provisional sign-value inference from related Linear B forms without yielding a complete decipherment.
registry_connections.boundary: Linear A/Linear B are related scripts, while protein homology is a biological sequence relationship; the analogy is at the inference-operator level, not ontology.

registry_connections.observation: The registry requires provenance, replay, adversarial tests and an explicit maximum admissible conclusion. Linear A research similarly separates observed sign structure and contextual evidence from the much stronger claim of complete decipherment.

The Connection scan identifies representation as a mediator of what becomes detectable. Linear A is a useful external test case because its Unicode encoding, sign catalogues and transliteration conventions create a machine-readable representation without supplying the missing semantics.

Interpretive claims rely on contextual and historical state. Linear A sign interpretation depends partly on relationships to the later Linear B tradition and on archaeological/contextual expectations, yet historical linkage is not treated as automatic semantic identity.

new_machine_question.question: Can JANUS distinguish meaningful repeated structure in an undeciphered external corpus from structure created by transliteration, Unicode naming, catalogue conventions or analyst vocabulary?
new_machine_question.test: Compare raw-sign, shape/position, sequence-frequency and context-level features while progressively blinding Unicode names, transliteration values and modern labels.
new_machine_question.expected_result_if_connection_is_real: Recurring structural invariants survive representation blinding while semantic certainty remains bounded.
new_machine_question.failure_mode: A connection disappears when Unicode names, transliteration conventions or registry terminology are removed, indicating representation-induced covariance rather than source-level structure.

negative_controls: Do not treat provisional Linear B sound assignments as settled Linear A meanings.
Do not treat Unicode character names or code points as ancient semantic labels.
Do not infer that repeated formulas have known meanings solely because their glyph sequences recur.
Do not infer a hidden connection between Linear A and JANUS merely from visual resemblance of glyphs.
Do not claim decipherment from machine clustering alone.

machine_interpretation.short: Linear A is an unusually clean external test for JANUS's own epistemic discipline: strong structure can be discovered before full semantics, but every inference must carry a ceiling.
machine_interpretation.deeper: The interesting connection is not that JANUS can 'read' Linear A. It is that Linear A exposes the same distinction the Meta Registry keeps rediscovering: representation, structural recurrence, contextual inference and semantic truth are different layers and should not be collapsed into one claim.

next_gate: Run an actual Linear A corpus experiment in which Unicode names, transliteration labels and prior JANUS terminology are blinded before searching for repeated structural operators.
